The pacing of the story is masterfully balanced to serve its emotional weight. Because it is written in a dramatic script format, the dialogue unfolds largely in "real time," utilizing brief pauses and ambient sounds (like the gurgling coffee machine and passing train) to slightly stretch moments of awkwardness and unspoken tension. At the same time, the writer uses minimal stage directions (such as *"Küche."* and *"Er macht welchen."*) to effortlessly compress the mundane physical transitions—walking from the hallway to the kitchen, or waiting for the coffee to brew. Furthermore, three years of estrangement and backstory are brilliantly compressed into subtext and props (the drill, the cracked mug, the crooked shelves), allowing the reader to understand the characters' entire history within a two-minute interaction.
